B is worried or appears worried
B does not have the real facts

decisions.claim: B is currently standing or not seated
decisions.reason: 'Please sit down' presupposes B is not currently seated; this is a standard presupposition of the directive 'sit down'.

decisions.claim: B has been finger-pointing or is finger-pointing
decisions.reason: 'You should avoid finger-pointing' does not strictly presuppose B has been finger-pointing. 'Avoid' can be preemptive advice (e.g., 'avoid jaywalking' doesn't mean the person has jaywalked). The conditional 'when you haven't got the real facts' further weakens any entailment of prior action.
decisions.counterexample: A could be giving general behavioral advice about a situation B is discussing rather than accusing B of having finger-pointed.
